From exclusive networking events and startup showcases to happy hours, dinners, and after-hours meetups, discover what’s happening across San Francisco during Disrupt Week, October 10–16. Find your next connection, your next opportunity, or your next favorite event.
articles.summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is just the beginning, with additional events in San Francisco offering networking opportunities, startup showcases, and social gatherings.
points: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 includes more than just the main event with various side events and networking opportunities.
Exclusive networking events and startup showcases provide platforms for startups and entrepreneurs.
Social gatherings like happy hours, dinners, and after-hours meetups facilitate informal interactions and connections.
articles.insight: The multitude of side events at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 reflects the industry's emphasis on networking and community-building, offering invaluable opportunities for startups to establish connections and partnerships.

articles.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 starts in 4 days — lock in your pass savings of up to $100 before prices rise
articles.description: Four days until TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 starts, when 10,000 founders, investors, and tech leaders gather in San Francisco's Moscone West on October 13-15. Save up to $100 on your price. Plus, save 50% on a second pass of the same type.
articles.summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will begin in four days, bringing together 10,000 attendees for the event. The article promotes early registration to secure savings on event tickets and additional discounts for a second pass.
points: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 event starts on October 13, attracting tech enthusiasts and leaders.
Early bird tickets can be purchased for up to $100 off, with additional discounts for a second pass.
The event is happening in San Francisco's Moscone West, indicating a significant gathering of the tech community.
articles.insight: This promotion indicates that the event organizers are trying to maximize attendance by offering substantial ticket discounts. This could reflect the growing importance and competitiveness of the tech industry events market.

articles.title: Xona’s commercial GPS alternative is about to go live
articles.description: Xona's precision timing and navigation service will enter beta testing after SpaceX launches six satellites designed by the company.
articles.summary: Xona is launching six satellites designed by the company for a precision timing and navigation service which will enter beta testing.
points: Xona's precision timing and navigation service is entering beta testing after the SpaceX satellite launch.
The launch will involve SpaceX launching six satellites that were designed by Xona.
This service could potentially serve as a commercial alternative to GPS.
articles.insight: The launch of Xona's satellites and subsequent beta testing of their precision timing and navigation service could provide a viable commercial alternative to GPS technology, potentially disrupting the industry.

articles.title: President Trump awards big tech donors with nation’s highest science prizes
articles.description: On Thursday, President Trump awarded Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and AMD’s Lisa Su the National Medal of Science, the nation’s top science prize.
articles.summary: President Trump awarded the National Medal of Science to tech moguls Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and Lisa Su from AMD for their contributions to technology and science.
points: President Trump awarded the National Medal of Science to four prominent figures in the technology industry.
The recipients included tech entrepreneurs Elon Musk and Jensen Huang, as well as Sergey Brin from Google and Lisa Su from AMD.
The award recognized the substantial impact of these individuals on advancing technology and science.
articles.insight: The recognition of prominent technology figures with the nation's highest science prize indicates the growing intersection of technology and national scientific achievement and the importance of private sector contributions to scientific progress.

articles.title: Pretend you’re sitting at Elizabeth Holmes’ desk on this weirdly detailed website
articles.description: With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents from the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to rifle through the Theranos founder's desk.
articles.summary: Extend engineer Bo Lau has crafted a website simulating Elizabeth Holmes' desk during the US v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, showcasing her personal and professional items, some of which are controversial.
points: A website has been created featuring over a thousand items from Elizabeth Holmes' desk.
The site includes personal items, professional artifacts, and some controversial items.
The website provides a vivid snapshot of Holmes' life and work during the trial.
articles.insight: This website sheds light on the personal and professional world of Elizabeth Holmes, providing a unique perspective on her role and actions in the Theranos case, with implications for understanding the culture and practices within Silicon Valley's tech industry.

articles.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims, warn of chilling effect
articles.description: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute allegations of mishandling sensitive information, warning in an open letter that their dismissals are creating a chilling effect on the company’s AI safety culture.
articles.summary: Three OpenAI safety researchers who were recently fired dispute allegations of misconCT, claiming their dismissals are harming the AI safety culture. They warn that fear of repercussions could stifle essential safety research and open discussion.
points: Three OpenAI safety researchers disputed their firings, alleging misconduct.
They claim their dismissals are damaging AI safety culture and inhibiting necessary discussions.
OpenAI's response to the disputes is not mentioned in the article.
articles.insight: The dismissal of the OpenAI safety researchers could have a detrimental impact on the AI safety culture by instilling fear and hindering open dialogue and research within the organization.
